Free connection tools
SSH, Mosh and local terminal
Remote shell access plus a shell on the desktop machine
SFTP, Telnet and serial
File transfers and access to compatible legacy equipment
Tunnels, chains and proxies
Reach private services through an approved network path

Jump hosts, proxies, agent forwarding and serial became free in desktop 10.1.0, September 2026. Device and server support still apply.

Host organization
Groups
Use projects, clients or environments as the hierarchy
Inherited settings
Share credentials, routing, environment and appearance defaults
Tags and search
Find related machines without duplicating host entries

Nested groups can supply settings to hosts unless overridden. Tags provide another search dimension. Changing a group can affect many connections.

Port forwarding and routing
Local
Use a local listener to reach a service through an SSH host
Remote
Forward a server-side listener toward a client-side service
Dynamic
Provide a SOCKS endpoint for compatible applications

Example only: 127.0.0.1:15432 on a laptop tunnels through a bastion to db.internal:5432. Server forwarding policy and endpoint reachability still apply.

SFTP in the same workflow
Browse, transfer and edit files beside the terminal

Desktop provides two panes; mobile supports multiple SFTP tabs. File editing downloads a copy and tracks changes for upload. Filesystem permissions and distribution sandboxing still apply.

Credentials and authentication
Reusable identities, certificates and device-backed keys

SSH keys and certificates, FIDO2 and biometrics are documented. SSH ID publishes public keys while keeping private keys device-bound. Server provisioning and revocation are separate responsibilities.

Desktop workspaces
Focus view, split sessions and reusable layouts

At least two sessions are required. Templates capture connection and layout state. They should not be treated as guaranteed persistent remote processes.

Snippets and broadcast
Saved commands
Keep inspection commands and scripts in reusable packages
Multi-execution and broadcast
Send a script or input to several intended destinations
Startup snippets
Run an assigned command when a connection opens

Basic snippets and multi-execution appear in Starter. Startup snippets require Pro or above. Check destinations and current shell state before broadcasting.

Autocomplete and AI
Completion
Suggestions from paths, history, commands and snippets
Natural language
Generate a candidate command or a saved snippet
Review before execution
Check paths and effects; avoid submitting secrets in prompts

Shell integration is local Bash/Zsh and documented remotely for Bash with OpenSSH 7.2+. It may disconnect servers that reject extra exec channels. Command generation is described as cloud processing. Current AI quotas were not verified.

Synchronization and vault protection
Across devices
Keep an eligible personal vault available on desktop and mobile
Local credentials option
Exclude personal keys and identities from synchronization
Recovery boundary
Preserve the encryption password and any unsynced changes

Personal credential sync can be disabled separately. Other eligible vault data continues syncing. Logout clears local data; unsynced changes after expiry can be lost. SSO does not replace the vault encryption password.

Session logs and bookmarks
Review a session and preserve the important ones

Recent logs rotate per host. Bookmarks preserve selected sessions. Mosh is not recorded. Mobile records but cannot view logs. Disabling logging deletes the vault’s logs, including bookmarks.

Team collaboration
Shared infrastructure
Make host settings and approved scripts available together
Live terminal work
Troubleshoot together with controlled typing handoff
Shared records
Review recent per-host, per-member sessions and comments

Owners manage membership and vault access. The homepage describes multiplayer with one typist at a time. The pricing table lists multiplayer as free, while team-wide sharing is paid; exact account limits need confirmation.

Business access and SSO
Separate vaults
Give each project or environment its own access boundary
Viewer and editor
Distinguish connecting from editing stored infrastructure data
Identity provider login
Centralize sign-in while retaining a vault encryption password

Multiple vaults can separate clients or environments. Viewer permissions still allow connections and snippets; server privileges remain independent. SAML is a Business add-on and included in the Enterprise pricing summary.

Cloud inventory eligibility is disputed
Pricing table: Pro+   •   Implementation guides: Team+

All three integration guides specify Team, Business and Enterprise. The pricing table includes cloud integration in Pro. Confirm eligibility before buying for this feature. Azure excludes VMs without public IPs.

Operational limits worth checking
Compatibility
Shell integration, cryptographic algorithms and app sandboxing
Data retention
Rotating logs, deleted logs and local-only credentials
Access revocation
Remove server permissions as well as client vault membership

Test each requirement on a non-production host with the intended app version and distribution. These are documented limitations, not results from a hands-on test.

Plan selection

Assessment: choose the lowest plan that meets a tested workflow. The free tier can cover substantial single-device use. Student eligibility may provide Pro and Team features through GitHub.

A short evaluation workflow
Connect and organize
Create two groups, assign a key and verify a host
Work across tools
Transfer a sample file, open a workspace and start a local tunnel
Validate the paid need
Test sync, log bookmarks and separate vault permissions

Use disposable or non-production hosts. Record OS, app version, distribution and subscription. No commands in this presentation have been executed against your systems.
